title: Automated dist-parity spec: fail when committed dist/ is stale vs source
description:
During the discovery-first init epic-let, dist/init.cjs was left STALE after TASK-045 and TASK-046 (the developers changed bundled source — src/project-md.js, src/question-library.js, src/agent-generator.js, bin/init.js — but did not rebuild the committed bundle). The full test:all suite passed GREEN anyway because there is no automated check that the committed dist/*.cjs matches a fresh build. The stale bundle was caught only by a live end-to-end run by the orchestrator; without that, the shipped /init-project command and CLI would have run old code in users' projects.

Add a permanent sensor so this can never silently ship again: a spec (or a CI/precommit check) that rebuilds the plugin bundles and fails if the committed dist/ differs from the fresh build. The repo already relies on this invariant informally (prior decisions note 'reviewer checks git diff --stat dist/ empty' as a MANUAL step) — this ticket makes it an automated gate.

Design notes / open questions for the implementer:
- The check must run `npm run build:plugin` (or invoke esbuild equivalently) into a temp/throwaway output and byte-compare against the committed dist/*.cjs (init.cjs, new-task.cjs, mcp-server.cjs, task-board.cjs — whatever build:plugin emits), rather than mutating the working tree.
- Decide tier placement: this is slow (spawns a build), so it belongs in the e2e/slow tier and/or the release gate, NOT the fast inner loop. Consider gating it to run only in test:all to keep test:changed fast.
- Beware environment non-determinism in esbuild output (banner, paths). If byte-equality is flaky, compare a normalized form or a content hash of the emitted modules.
- This is test/release infrastructure, so the ticket itself runs the full test:all gate.
acceptance_criteria: A new automated check rebuilds the plugin bundle(s) via the project's build pipeline into a non-committed location and compares the result against the committed dist/*.cjs; it FAILS when they differ (i.e. when a source change was not accompanied by a dist rebuild).
The check is placed in the slow/release tier (runs under npm run test:all and/or a release/precommit gate), NOT in the fast inner loop (test:changed / test:watch stay fast).

A deliberate proof: temporarily editing a bundled source file without rebuilding makes the check FAIL (red), and rebuilding makes it PASS (green) — demonstrating the sensor is non-vacuous (document this red-green proof, do not leave the source edit committed).
Any esbuild output non-determinism (banners, absolute paths) is handled so the check is stable across machines (byte-compare a normalized form or a content hash, with the normalization documented).

Docs/policy updated: the CLAUDE.md or state note that previously described the 'reviewer checks git diff --stat dist/ empty' MANUAL step references the new automated gate; npm run test:all stays green.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: Plan + tier: verification_tier=tests-after, BUT this is test/release infrastructure → the FULL test:all gate applies (per the policy clause: any ticket touching test infra runs test:all). Design locked: refactor scripts/build-plugin.mjs to accept an OUTPUT-DIR override (env var, default dist/ — default behavior byte-unchanged) so the parity spec rebuilds with the SAME esbuild config (single source of truth, NOT a duplicated options block in the test). The spec (slow tier, tests/e2e/) builds all four bundles (init/new-task/mcp-server/task-board) into a mkdtemp dir and byte-compares each against the committed dist/<name>; fails on any diff. Slow tier by directory so the fast inner loop (test:changed/test:watch) stays fast. Red-green proof required (edit a bundled source without rebuilding → red; rebuild → green) per AC3 — the sensor must be provably non-vacuous (the red-green-plant standing practice for new static locks). esbuild is deterministic for a pinned version + same cwd; byte-compare should hold, but handle any cwd-relative-path comment non-determinism (normalize + document) if it surfaces. Single IMPL phase (tests-after).

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body: APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS (0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 2 LOW). All 5 ACs verified fresh. Independently reproduced the RED on TWO source files (not trusting the dev): a string-literal edit to src/project-md.js (no rebuild) → spec FAILED naming exactly dist/init.cjs; an edit to src/task-store.js (bundled by all four) → spec FAILED naming ALL FOUR bundles — confirms the spec accumulates every mismatch into drifted[] and asserts once, not bail-on-first. Reverted both, tree clean, spec green. Determinism: spec spawns the build with cwd=REPO_ROOT sharing the buildTo() export (one esbuild code path for both builds); 2 isolation runs byte-stable; not self-referential (builds working-tree source, compares to committed dist — proven by the RED reproductions). Default build byte-unchanged: npm run build:plugin → git diff --stat dist/ EMPTY. AC5 CLAUDE.md note present + accurate. Full gate test:all 583 passed / 4 skipped. 2 LOW (both authorized for in-band fix): (1) BUNDLE_NAMES hand-duplicated vs the exported ENTRYPOINT_NAMES — a 5th bundle would be silently unchecked + false single-source-of-truth comment; (2) inaccurate red-green evidence comment claiming new-task.cjs bundles project-md.js (it does not).

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: CLOSED — done on green review (APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS, 0 HIGH/0 MEDIUM; both LOWs fixed in-band, not deferred). Linked commits: 97702c4 (impl: build-plugin.mjs OUTPUT-DIR override + buildTo()/ENTRYPOINT_NAMES exports + tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js + CLAUDE.md note) + aa147e6 (review fixes: spec imports ENTRYPOINT_NAMES so the parity check auto-covers any future 5th bundle; corrected evidence comment). Verified in-band fix myself: ENTRYPOINT_NAMES wired, parity spec green 2/2, dist clean. The stale-dist gap that bit 045/046 is now an automated release-tier gate — npm run test:all fails if committed dist/*.cjs (all four bundles) drifts from a fresh build. Red-green-proven non-vacuous (reviewer independently reproduced). The manual 'git diff --stat dist/ empty' reviewer step is retired in favor of this sensor (CLAUDE.md updated). Backlog now drained of actionable tickets — only TASK-003 (Jira) remains, blocked on Atlassian creds.
